passage: When the teacher read out "First prize: Soo-ah," the whole class in Lisbon clapped, and Paulo clapped too. His hands were moving, but his stomach felt tight. Soo-ah was his best friend. She had spent three weekends on her drawing of a lighthouse. He was proud of her, and he also wished his own painting of a bus had been picked. After class he walked up to her. "Your lighthouse was really good," he said, and he meant it. That night he took out a fresh sheet and began drawing buses again, this time practising windows and shadows, the way Soo-ah had practised waves.

qa.q: What did Soo-ah draw for the prize?
What was Paulo feeling while he clapped?
qa.a: He felt proud of his best friend and jealous at the same time; the tight stomach shows the sting even while his hands clapped. 🤔

qa.q: How did Paulo turn the sting into something useful?
qa.a: He congratulated Soo-ah honestly and then practised his own drawing, working on windows and shadows.

qa.q: How might Soo-ah see Paulo's words after class?
qa.a: She probably felt happy that her best friend was glad for her, and she may not have known about the sting he felt.

grounding: Paulo feels jealousy and pride together about a best friend's prize, congratulates her and uses it to practise more.
